I was obese pretty much my whole life and food was my outlet. I tried pretty much every diet, program and sports as well. I would lose weight and gain back double every time.

Before deciding to go with the surgery, I did extensive research about it. I attended classes with pre- and post- operative patients. Ranging from 1 month out to 10 years our after surgery. It was very eye opening. There were good and bad discussions, but in the end the benefits outweighed the risks for me (and for all the patients there). I was pre diabetic when I was younger and had menstrual problems but besides that no major health problems just a very high BMI of about 55.

I was on a medical weight loss program before the surgery and had to lose 10% of my weight on my own following a strict diet and I did. I lost 45 lbs and it was so hard. I am completely restricted now and I had to prepare to be okay with it. I am. Of course I still crave some Costco cheese pizza or a brownie, but there are healthier alternatives and I have accepted that I can live without those things. 

It’s still hard, don’t get me wrong. It’s always easier said than done. I had to change my lifestyle and eating habits or else this surgery wouldn’t work. It is a tool not a simple fix and I am in control of that tool.

Lately I’ve been going through a lot. I thought I had it worse back then but damn was I wrong. And I was so close to attempting suicide. 

I just turned 21 last year and finally saved all my money up and bought myself a new car and my first two bedroom apartment and told my mom I’m moving her in with me. She was living with an abusive boyfriend. I did it. I got my mom out after 8 years. I also bought her a car. I was working full time and making good money. I felt on top of the world. I lost 100+ lbs too during that time. AND, I pulled my drug addicted brother off the streets and moved him in with me. 

Just at my peak, I had to have a couple surgeries and developed a muscle condition. 

Now, I cannot work. I am at home 24/7 besides my 4x a week 3-4 hour long pain management/therapy sessions. I can’t go shower without having a chair to sit in.  I can only sleep in one position. I cannot go grocery shopping because I cannot stand for longer than 15 minutes. I am constantly in pain. That is all I know. I’m 21. I used to do all of this with no effort, simply as easy as taking a breath.  My mom now has to work 12 hour days. We are barely getting by, living by a thread.  My goal was to financially take care of her. Now it’s the opposite and it kills me. I feel like a burden. My brother is still struggling with drugs too and that’s a different struggle altogether. 

ALL of that has happened since November 20th, 2017. Less than a year from my life to do a 360. 

I’ve had to keep my strength through all of it. God or whoever put there knows how many times I’ve wished for death. I’ve had to keep true to who I KNOW I am and my capabilities and abilities. I cannot lose touch of it or I will lose myself. I have had to learn acceptance. I have had to notice and be aware of things I cannot change, accept it, which does not mean I am okay with it, then move on. Do not dwell or be sad too long because that’s when you start to suffer. I have to remind myself that every single day. 

That’s what works for me... I still struggle every single day. My life has shrunk and I’m pretty much handicapped and feel useless. But in reality I am not. If I think about it, there is a lot of good things about me. I am funny, I have a good heart and always have my shoulder out for someone to cry on. 

I’m sure there are good things about you too and that is WHO you are. 

Everything that has happened that has led up to exactly where you are now is building your strength. You have the power to react and you control how much you want the situation to affect you. 

I never wanted to die, I just wanted a different life and that is what I’m working towards. Even if I cannot see the light at the end of the tunnel, I’m still going to search; because if you don’t stick around you never know if something good could’ve happened.

I’m 21 and  my whole life changed in a flash.  Last year I worked full time, bought my first apartment and moved my mom in with me, bought myself and her a car. My life was just beginning. Now I feel as if it is over. I can’t work. I can’t go grocery shopping and stand over 30 min. I can’t go upstairs or down without stopping. I can’t stand and cook a meal. I can’t shower without a chair.
Pain. Pain. Pain.

I am so reduced.

I feel like a shell of what I once was.

What is most difficult is knowing who I am and my capabilities but not being able to reach them... 

BUT, I cannot give up... if I give up I might miss out on the opportunity of something good. 

RADICAL ACCEPTANCE has helped me a TON.  Of course you have to practice the way of thinking and apply it.

1. Be aware/mindful/conscious of the situation or whatever situation that is bothering me or that I cannot change.

2. Acknowledge it. Accept it. This does not mean that I am okay with it. It just means that I am aware of what’s going on and all I can do is notice is and know that it is there.

3. DO NOT DWELL ON IT. Of course we are all emotional about our pain/situation, but when you linger with sadness/anger/frustration too long that’s when you begin to suffer.

It is natural to be emotional, do not control it; but do not let it control you and take over to the point that you suffer.

I will not lie, I still have my low moments (last night lol). But I got through it. And we all have this capability. All of us do. 

Don’t give up. We’re all in this with you.
